Every class begins at the barre. Every dancer leaves a little taller.

Founded in 2012 by Mira Ostrowska, Suzu Ballet is a daylight studio in Victoria dedicated to deliberate, classical dance training for students of all ages. We believe that proper alignment is built through patient repetition and hands-on corrections rather than hurried routines. In our two light-filled rooms, the Window Studio and the Garden Studio, students practise on sprung maple floors that protect the body while building strength and poise.

Every adult and Juniors class is accompanied by a live pianist, grounding technique in responsive acoustic music. From four-year-olds in Pre-ballet discovering balance to adults refining their adage, our dancers share a quiet, focused room where disciplined study produces genuine grace.

OUR STUDIO →

Three pillars of our practice

Live piano, every adult class

Acoustic music teaches dancers how to breathe within the phrase, adjusting tempo and dynamics to support the work at the barre and in the centre.

Small classes: 12 children, 16 adults

We cap attendance at twelve students for children and sixteen for adults, so every dancer receives personal, hands-on corrections from the teacher during each exercise.

One studio, ages 4 to 70+

Children, teenagers and adult dancers share the same sprung floors and natural daylight, a multi-generational community united by a shared dedication to classical technique.

CLASSES
& FEES

Children from 4, adults at any age

We offer structured training in four divisions: Pre-ballet for ages 4 to 6, Children for ages 7 to 10, Juniors for ages 11 to 15, and adult classes from Beginners to Open level. Whether you commit to a twelve-week term or drop in for morning practice, you can begin with a trial class for $15.

CLASSES & FEES →

THE WEEK,
MORNING TO NIGHT

MORNING · WEEKDAYS 07:00–11:15

The barre, divided

The studio wakes in clear daylight for the 75-minute Morning Open Class and the daytime Adult Beginners. Mira divides the class with classical rigour: 40 minutes at the barre through pliés, tendus, ronds de jambe, fondus, frappés, adage and grands battements, then 25 minutes of centre work and allegro, closing with a 5-minute révérence. At the piano, Hélène gives each exercise its own character: a slow 3/4 for pliés, a crisp 2/4 for tendus, a lively mazurka for ronds de jambe and a broad waltz for grands battements.

As the afternoon light shifts, younger dancers fill the studios. In the Garden Studio, Aiko introduces four- to six-year-olds to posture, skips and rhythm in Pre-ballet. At 17:30 Tomás welcomes the Juniors into the Window Studio for classical training with Daniel at the piano, building strength, turn-out and precision at the barre.

pages.title: Classes
pages.content:
CLASSES

Classes for Every Age

Suzu Ballet offers structured training for young children, developing dancers, and adults of all experience levels in Victoria. Every class is capped for personal attention and accompanied by focused musicality.

Pre-Ballet and Children

Pre-ballet introduces children aged 4 to 6 to rhythm, spatial awareness, and basic ballet positions in the Garden Studio. Classes run for 45 minutes once a week, capped strictly at 12 dancers to ensure each child receives gentle guidance. Dancers wear a simple leotard or T-shirt with leggings and soft ballet shoes or socks; uniform is never required. The 12-week term fee is $180. For ages 7 to 10, the Children programme deepens classical technique with two 60-minute classes weekly for $300 per 12-week term, also capped at 12 students. Both levels are taught by Aiko Brandt with focused musical care.

Juniors Programme

Our Juniors programme is designed for dancers aged 11 to 15 who are ready for rigorous technical foundation and classical vocabulary. Meeting in the Window Studio three times weekly for 90 minutes per session, the class is taught by Tomás Ferreira with live piano accompaniment by Daniel Mensah. Dancers work on placement, strength, allegro, and preparatory pointe readiness. Class size is limited to 12 students to maintain direct teacher corrections at the barre and in the centre. Students wear plain dancewear or leggings and soft shoes. The fee is $480 per 12-week term. Interested dancers may book a trial class for $15.

Adult Ballet Classes

Adult classes welcome dancers at every stage of life, from absolute beginners to experienced dancers returning after decades. Daytime and evening Adult Beginners sessions focus on posture, alignment, and basic barre exercises under Priya Raman with live piano. Adult Improvers builds complex combinations, turns, and musical phrasing. Intermediate and advanced dancers gather for Morning Open Class with founder Mira Ostrowska and pianist Hélène Marchetti, or Saturday Adult Open. Adult classes run 75 to 90 minutes and are capped at 16 dancers. Wear comfortable clothing you can move in freely. Options include a $24 drop-in, a $200 10-class card, or a $165 unlimited month.

TIMETABLE

The Week at Suzu

Our studio operates six days a week across two daylight rooms, with classes accompanied by live piano for all adults and Juniors. The school year is divided into three 12-week terms, and we close on statutory holidays.

Weekday Morning and Daytime Schedule

From Monday to Friday, mornings begin in the Window Studio with Morning Open Class for intermediate and advanced adults from 07:00 to 08:15, taught by Mira Ostrowska with Hélène Marchetti at the piano. On Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, daytime Adult Beginners meet from 10:00 to 11:15 with Priya Raman and Hélène Marchetti. In the afternoon, younger dancers arrive in the Garden Studio: Pre-ballet for ages 4 to 6 runs Monday and Wednesday from 15:45 to 16:30 with Aiko Brandt, while Children aged 7 to 10 meet Tuesday and Thursday from 16:30 to 17:30 with Aiko Brandt.

Evening and Saturday Classes

Evening sessions in the Window Studio feature live accompaniment by Daniel Mensah. On Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, Juniors aged 11 to 15 train from 17:30 to 19:00 with Tomás Ferreira. Adult Improvers take the barre Monday and Wednesday from 19:15 to 20:30 with Priya Raman, while evening Adult Beginners meet Tuesday and Thursday from 19:15 to 20:30 with Priya Raman. On Wednesday and Friday from 20:30 to 21:30 during the Spring term, the Repertory rehearsal convenes by invitation in the Garden Studio with Tomás Ferreira and Daniel Mensah. Saturdays feature Pre-ballet from 09:00 to 09:45, Children from 10:00 to 11:00, and Saturday Adult Open from 11:15 to 12:45 with Mira and Hélène.

pages.title: Teachers & Pianists
pages.content:
TEACHERS & PIANISTS

Teachers and Pianists

Teaching at Suzu Ballet combines decades of classical performance with sensitive, individual instruction. Our faculty and studio accompanists work together daily in our Victoria studios.

Artistic Direction and Teaching Faculty

Founder and artistic director Mira Ostrowska established Suzu Ballet in 2012 following 14 years of professional dancing with touring companies. Mira leads Morning Open Class from Monday to Friday and Saturday Adult Open, bringing quiet precision and postural alignment to every barre. Tomás Ferreira teaches our Juniors programme and directs the Spring Repertory rehearsals with rigorous classical clarity and careful technical staging. Aiko Brandt leads Pre-ballet and Children classes, creating an imaginative, disciplined atmosphere where young dancers develop coordination and joy. Priya Raman instructs adult dancers across daytime Beginners, evening Beginners, and Adult Improvers, guiding newcomers and returning dancers with patient anatomical precision.

Pianists and Studio Management

Live music is fundamental to our teaching philosophy. Hélène Marchetti plays for all morning adult classes and Saturday sessions, adapting classical scores into nuanced tempos that breathe with the dancers' pliés, tendus, and adages. Daniel Mensah accompanies our evening adult classes, Juniors sessions, and Repertory rehearsals, providing rich dynamic phrasing that supports allegro and dramatic choreography. Front desk manager Lena Hofmann coordinates studio life, managing enrolments, trial class scheduling, and parent communications from Monday morning through Saturday afternoon. Together, our seven staff members ensure every dancer experiences a supportive, musically vibrant, and beautifully maintained studio environment every single day.

Two pianists, five teachers

Hélène Marchetti and Daniel Mensah play for every adult and Juniors class.

pages.title: Trial class
pages.content:
TRIAL CLASS

Your First Class

Taking a trial class gives you the chance to experience our daylight rooms, sprung maple floors, and live piano accompaniment firsthand. Any class across our schedule can be booked once for $15.

The Four-Step Trial Process

We have kept our trial procedure calm and straightforward. First, book online or call front desk manager Lena Hofmann at +1 250 555 0142. Second, arrive 15 minutes early at our Alder Row studio so we can show you the changing room, store your belongings, and assign your barre spot. Third, take the class, working at your own comfortable pace alongside our regular students and live pianist. Fourth, talk directly with the teacher after class about your experience, placement, and term options. Children may wear a leotard or T-shirt with leggings and soft shoes or socks. Adults should wear any comfortable athletic clothing that allows ease of movement.

What should I wear to my trial class?

You do not need specialised dance uniform or professional shoes for a trial class at Suzu Ballet. For adults, comfortable workout wear such as leggings, yoga trousers, or a fitted T-shirt works perfectly, paired with soft ballet slippers or clean socks. For children in Pre-ballet or Children classes, a simple leotard or a plain T-shirt with leggings and socks or ballet flats is ideal. Hair should be tied neatly back from the face so you can balance and spot turns comfortably.

Do I need previous dance experience?

No previous ballet background is required to attend our trial class. Our daytime and evening Adult Beginners sessions are created specifically for people stepping into a dance studio for the first time or returning after years away. Teachers introduce every term and movement methodically from the barre outward, breaking down alignment, weight transfer, and terminology in accessible language. If you have danced before, a trial class allows our teachers to evaluate your technique and recommend Adult Improvers or Morning Open Class.

How early should I arrive for my appointment?

We ask all trial students to arrive exactly 15 minutes before class begins. This quiet buffer gives front desk manager Lena Hofmann time to welcome you, confirm your registration details, introduce you to the changing rooms, and show you where dance bags are placed. It also allows you to enter the studio room early, meet the teacher, adjust your barre height, and settle your breathing on our sprung maple floor before the piano starts.

How many students will be in the class?

Every class at Suzu Ballet is capped to ensure ample personal space and thorough feedback. Children's and Juniors classes are strictly limited to 12 students, while adult classes accommodate a maximum of 16 dancers. These small group sizes ensure that the teacher can observe your lines, provide individualized corrections at the barre, and maintain safe distancing across the floor during moving combinations and allegro.

How do I book my trial session?

You can schedule your trial class by phoning our front desk directly at +1 250 555 0142 or emailing Lena Hofmann at hello@suzuballet.example. Let us know which day and level you are considering, and we will confirm availability in the Window Studio or Garden Studio. The single trial fee is $15 with no ongoing commitment required. If you decide to enrol, we will credit your trial experience toward your term.

pages.title: About the studio
pages.content:
ABOUT THE STUDIO

About the Studio

Founded in 2012 by Mira Ostrowska, Suzu Ballet is a dedicated classical studio in Victoria where children and adults share the same daylight spaces and sprung floors. We believe classical ballet belongs to anyone willing to work with patience and musical care.

Our Story and Artistic Philosophy

Mira Ostrowska founded Suzu Ballet in 2012 after fourteen years dancing professionally with touring companies. Having trained under rigorous classical traditions, she envisioned a calm, daylight school where technical honesty and healthy biomechanics were taught without vanity or harshness. Today, our school welcomes dancers from age 4 to over 70 under one roof at 210 Alder Row. We believe posture, balance, and expressive line are cultivated by hand, through consistent daily barre work and immediate personal feedback. Rather than preparing dancers for commercial competitions or commercial exams, we focus on genuine physical alignment, artistic understanding, and lifelong discipline.

The Studios, Flooring, and Live Piano

Our studio building features two distinct training spaces designed specifically for classical dance. The Window Studio is our primary room, defined by three tall arched windows that flood the room with morning light, a custom sprung maple floor that protects joints during landings, and an acoustic upright piano. The Garden Studio provides an intimate setting for Pre-ballet classes and evening Repertory staging. Live piano accompaniment by Hélène Marchetti and Daniel Mensah accompanies every adult and Juniors class. Having a live musician in the room teaches dancers to listen, breathe with musical phrasing, and respond dynamically to subtle shifts in tempo.

Small by design

12 children and 16 adults per class, live piano in every adult and Juniors class, two daylight rooms.

SINCE 2012

pages.title: Showcase
pages.content:
SHOWCASE

On Stage in June

The annual Suzu Ballet Showcase takes place every year on the second Saturday of June at a local community theatre hall. It offers our dancers an authentic theatrical culmination to their year of disciplined studio work.

The Annual June Showcase

On the second Saturday of June, Suzu Ballet gathers on stage for our annual school performance in a hired community theatre hall in Victoria. Participation is entirely voluntary: every class that wishes to perform presents a short choreographic piece developed during term time. Rather than stressful competitions or high-pressure galas, our showcase is designed as a calm, dignified celebration of musicality and technical progress. Dancers from Pre-ballet, Children, Juniors, and adult levels experience stage lighting, live backstage cues, and the shared pleasure of performing for family and fellow dancers. Costumes are lent directly by the school at no extra fee.

Spring Repertory Rehearsals

Preparation for the Showcase culminates during the Spring term with our dedicated Repertory group. Rehearsals take place by invitation on Wednesday and Friday evenings from 20:30 to 21:30 in the Garden Studio under the direction of teacher Tomás Ferreira and pianist Daniel Mensah. During these intensive hour-long sessions, dancers learn classical excerpts, refine corps de ballet spacing, and polish ensemble timing. Working closely with Daniel's live accompaniment allows dancers to deepen their musical sensitivity and theatrical stamina. If you are interested in joining future showcase pieces or learning more about rehearsal commitments, speak with your class instructor or front desk manager Lena Hofmann.

Second Saturday of June

Every class that wishes to perform presents a short piece. No competition, no pressure.

EVERY JUNE

pages.title: Journal
pages.content:
JOURNAL

Journal from the Studio

Notes, essays, and seasonal announcements from our daylight studios at 210 Alder Row. Here we record the quiet progress of our students, technical observations, and studio news.

Stories from the Barre

Our journal documents real experiences from daily life at Suzu Ballet. In 'Back at the barre at 41,' adult student Nora Whitfield reflects on returning to Adult Improvers after twenty years away, rediscovering posture, physical confidence, and focus. In 'Six months to the first pointe shoes,' teacher Tomás Ferreira explains how strength, ankle alignment, and core stability determine pointe readiness for Juniors, proving that physical readiness rather than chronological age must always guide the transition. In 'What the pianist plays for pliés,' studio accompanist Hélène Marchetti shares excerpts from her notebook of tempos, demonstrating how specific musical meters support classical exercises at the barre.

Studio Notices and Announcements

Stay informed regarding term dates, seasonal workshops, and studio maintenance schedules. Enrolment is currently open for our three 12-week terms commencing in September, January, and April. Registration is handled directly through front desk manager Lena Hofmann, and class sizes remain strictly capped at 12 children and 16 adults. We are also pleased to announce our upcoming summer intensive programme, offering focused weekday training for Juniors and adult dancers. Please note our annual studio closure during the final week of August, when our sprung maple floors in both the Window Studio and Garden Studio receive their regular maintenance and oiling.

CONTACT

Contact and Visit

Suzu Ballet is situated on Alder Row in downtown Victoria, welcoming students and visitors six days a week. We are happy to assist with class placement, term enrolments, and trial scheduling.

Studio Location and Hours

Our studio is located on the 2nd floor at 210 Alder Row, Victoria, BC V8W 1A1, Canada. The building is conveniently situated a 5-minute walk from major Douglas Street bus stops, with nearby street parking and bicycle stands. Our front desk is open Monday to Friday from 06:45 to 21:45 and Saturday from 08:30 to 13:00. We are closed on Sundays and statutory holidays. Visitors are welcome to visit our reception area during desk hours to view our facilities, observe the Window Studio and Garden Studio, and pick up term information from studio manager Lena Hofmann.

Get in Touch and Bookings

To book a $15 trial class or ask questions about term placement, telephone our desk at +1 250 555 0142 or send an email to hello@suzuballet.example. Studio manager Lena Hofmann personally handles all student inquiries, helping you choose the right class level and confirming your reservation. If you are enrolling a child, please let us know their age and any previous movement experience so we can recommend Pre-ballet or Children sessions. For adults, drop-in attendance ($24), 10-class cards ($200), and unlimited monthly passes ($165) can be arranged in person or by phone.

posts.title: Back at the barre at 41
posts.excerpt: After twenty years away from dance, Nora Whitfield returned to the barre in Adult Improvers at Suzu Ballet.
posts.content:
When Nora Whitfield stepped into the Window Studio on Alder Row on a wet Tuesday evening, it had been exactly twenty-one years since she last stood at a ballet barre. She was forty-one, working full days in Victoria, and carried the quiet physical hesitations common to anyone returning to an exacting physical discipline after decades away. Her soft ballet flats were new, bought the week before, and felt unusually thin against the pale sprung maple floor. Around her, dancers were stretching calves, warming ankles, or speaking quietly with pianist Daniel Mensah near the upright piano in the corner. There was neither fanfare nor judgment, only the soft creak of leather on timber and the pale wash of late afternoon light reflecting off the tall mirrors.

Nora had enrolled in Priya Raman’s Adult Improvers class on Monday and Wednesday evenings. In her teens, she had danced four afternoons a week, but university, career demands, and family responsibilities had gradually crowded out studio time. The idea of returning had lingered in her mind for years, tempered by the familiar worry that her joints would ache, her memory for combinations would falter, or she would feel hopelessly out of place among younger students. But Suzu Ballet does not operate like a conservatory audition or a commercial fitness boutique. With classes capped strictly at sixteen adult dancers, the room offers space to breathe, make mistakes, and listen to corrections without feeling scrutinised.

The class began with two hands on the barre for simple pliés in first position. When Daniel played a calm opening chord, Nora felt an immediate physical recognition that surprised her. Her heels pressed down into the maple boards, her spine lengthened upward through the crown of her head, and the familiar coordination of breath and bending knees returned as if stored beneath the skin. Priya moved quietly between dancers, offering gentle, manual corrections: adjusting a ribcage here, easing tension from a shoulder blade there, and reminding everyone to keep their weight over the balls of their feet.

As the barre progressed through tendus, ronds de jambe, and fondus, the physical demands became clearer. Tendons that had grown accustomed to sitting at office desks were asked to lengthen; stabilizing muscles around the hips and core were required to hold balance without gripping. Nora found herself sweating, not with the hurried strain of an aerobic gym workout, but with the quiet, internal heat that classical ballet demands. What struck her most was the presence of Daniel’s live piano. Rather than following an unyielding recorded track, Daniel watched the dancers’ heels and breaths, adjusting tempos slightly to give everyone time to finish an adage cleanly or close into fifth position.

By the time the class moved into the centre for port de bras and a modest allegro combination, Nora felt a renewed sense of posture and mental quiet. Standing tall between the barre and the tall arched windows, she realised that twenty years away had changed her body, but it had not diminished her capacity for discipline and grace. After class, while slipping on her coat by the wooden benches near the entrance, she spoke briefly with Priya about the term ahead. Nora was back at the barre, not to chase the dancer she was at eighteen, but to inhabit the strength and poise of who she is today.
